extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners (patent owners and third-party requesters), and other patent professionals involved in ex parte reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for conducting and responding to ex parte reexamination proceedings (including scope, prior art consideration, filings, claim treatment, and related procedural requirements). Targeted at USPTO examiners and practitioners preparing or responding to reexamination requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party-prepared papers not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: A federal district court does not have the authority to order a patent owner to file papers prepared by a third party in addition to the patent owner’s own submission in a patent reexamination proceeding; such papers prepared by the third party and filed by the patent owner will not be entered, and the entire submission will be returned as an inappropriate response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Emerson Elec. Co. v. Davoil, Inc.; see MPEP § 2266 and § 2267. Practitioners should not attempt to circumvent reexamination rules by filing third-party-prepared submissions through the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of reexamination proceedings (notification, special dispatch, scope of search)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination will be conducted in accordance with 37 CFR 1.104, 1.105, 1.110–1.113, and 1.116 (35 U.S.C. 132 and 133) and will result in issuance of a reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570; the proceeding shall be conducted with 'special dispatch' pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 305. A full search will not routinely be made by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party reexamination requester will be sent copies of Office actions and the patent owner must serve responses on the requester. Citations submitted prior to issuance of an order will be considered by the examiner. Reexamination will proceed even if the copy of the order sent to the patent owner is returned undelivered — 37 CFR 1.11(c) is constructive notice. See MPEP § 2230.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of examiner for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination will ordinarily be conducted by the same patent examiner who made the decision on whether the reexamination request should be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.515(c) is granted after an examiner's determination that the request did not raise any substantial new question (SNQ), the reexamination will generally be conducted by another examiner. See MPEP § 2236 and § 2248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of prior art to be considered (A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to further discussion in the section, the examiner must consider patents and printed publications: (A) cited by another reexamination requester under 37 CFR 1.510 or 1.915; (B) cited in a patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or a requester’s reply under 37 CFR 1.535 if they comply with 37 CFR 1.98; (C) cited by the patent owner under a duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.555) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.98; (D) discovered by the examiner in searching; (E) of record in the patent file from earlier examination; and (F) of record in the patent file from any 37 CFR 1.501 submission prior to date of an order if it complies with 37 CFR 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When parties submit documents in compliance with the rules, the degree of consideration normally depends on how well the submitting party explains content and relevance. Examiner initials adjacent to citations do not indicate substantive consideration beyond what is noted in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference copy requirements under 37 CFR 1.98
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2) requires a legible copy of: (1) each foreign patent; (2) each publication or that portion which caused it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office); (3) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims and any drawing of the application, or that portion which caused it to be listed; and (4) all other information or that portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings/applications (these may be mistaken for new requests); instead provide the application/proceeding number and status. The exception in 37 CFR 1.98(d)(1) does not apply to reexamination proceedings (no 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for submitting new art after NIRC (post-NIRC submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) has been mailed, a submission of patents/printed publications or other information after the NIRC has been mailed will not automatically delay prosecution or pull the proceeding from the printing process; to interrupt the process the submission must be accompanied by: (A) a factual accounting explaining why the information could not have been submitted earlier; (B) an unequivocal statement that one or more claims are unpatentable; and (C) an amendment to such claim(s) plus explanation how the amendment makes the claim(s) patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These must be provided via a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 (with petition fee). Requirements are similar to withdrawing an application from issue per 37 CFR 1.313(c). The Office requires such a basis to interrupt the proceeding and comply with statutory 'special dispatch' (35 U.S.C. 305).

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of prior art on official forms and citation list for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination request must provide a listing of the patents and printed publications as provided in 37 CFR 1.98. The examiner must list on form PTO-892, PTO/SB/08A or 08B, or PTO/SB/42 (or equivalent) all prior art patents or printed publications cited in the decision on the request, applied in making rejections, or cited as pertinent during proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All citations listed on form PTO-892 and all citations not lined-through on PTO/SB/08A/08B/42 (or equivalent) will be the list of prior art documents considered in the reexamination proceeding. A notice will be printed on the reexamination certificate that the cited prior art list will be available via PAIR by the reexamination control number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of submissions into reexamination certificate (how submissions are entitled to entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission of patents and/or publications is entitled to entry and citation in the reexamination certificate when it complies with 37 CFR 1.98 and is submitted: (A) by the patent owner in the statement under 37 CFR 1.530; (B) by the reexamination requester in the reply under 37 CFR 1.535; (C) prior to the order of reexamination under 37 CFR 1.501 by any party; and/or (D) by the patent owner under the duty of disclosure requirements of 37 CFR 1.555.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions not filed through the permitted avenues or not satisfying 1.98 may be returned, expunged, or discarded at the Office’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.552)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 37 CFR 1.552: (a) Claims will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted in the reexamination proceeding, on the basis of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112. (b) Claims will not be permitted to enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent. (c) Issues other than those in (a) and (b) will not be resolved in a reexamination proceeding (such issues should be considered via reissue). (d) Any statement of the patent owner and accompanying information submitted pursuant to § 1.501(a)(2) that is of record may be used after reexamination has been ordered to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim when applying patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other issues are raised during reexamination, the examiner should note them in the next Office action and advise the patent owner of the advisability of filing a reissue application for resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences for reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 (supplemental examination leading to ex parte reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.625(d) provides that any ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 will be conducted in accordance with §§ 1.530–1.570 except that: (1) the patent owner will not have the right to file a statement pursuant to § 1.530 nor will the order set a time period for such a statement; (2) reexamination of any claim may be conducted on the basis of any item of information in § 1.605 and is not limited to patents and printed publications; (3) issues in addition to those raised by patents/printed publications and added/deleted subject matter may be considered and resolved; and (4) information material to patentability will be defined by § 1.56(b), notwithstanding § 1.555(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 may therefore involve broader types of information (e.g., sales invoices, audio/video transcripts) and any ground of patentability (e.g., subject matter eligibility, anticipation, obviousness, written description, enablement, indefiniteness, double-patenting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 304: prior art limits, double patenting, and 35 U.S.C. 112 treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination proceeding ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 provides a complete reexamination of the patent claims on the basis of prior art patents and printed publications. Double patenting issues may also be considered. Issues relating to 35 U.S.C. 112 are addressed only with respect to new claims or amendatory subject matter in the specification, claims or drawings. Any new or amended claims are examined to ensure the scope of the original patent claims is not enlarged (35 U.S.C. 305).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double patenting may be considered both as a basis for ordering reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 304 and during subsequent examination on the merits; the examiner should determine whether double patenting raises a substantial new question of patentability and whether a double patenting rejection is appropriate during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable prior art regime (first-inventor-to-file vs first-to-invent) and effective date effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior art regime under which the application for the patent was examined (first-inventor-to-file or first-to-invent) will generally be applied in reexamination. If an amended or new claim has an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013, reexamination will be conducted under the first-inventor-to-file regime. If a benefit claim to a prior application with filing date before March 16, 2013 is made during reexamination, reexamination may be conducted under the first-to-invent regime only if the written description of the prior application provides adequate written support under 35 U.S.C. 112 for (1) all patent claims, (2) all claims presented at any time during prosecution of the application that matured into the patent, and (3) all claims presented at any time during prosecution of any application to which the benefit was sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art rejections under first-inventor-to-file are based on 35 U.S.C. 102 as in effect on/after March 16, 2013; under first-to-invent, rejections may be based on provisions of 35 U.S.C. 102 in effect prior to March 16, 2013 (including subsections (a), (b), (d), (e), (g) as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on basing rejections on matters other than patents/printed publications in reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections in reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 may only be made on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications; rejections will not be based on matters other than patents or printed publications, such as public use or sale, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101, conduct issues, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection on prior public use or sale or insufficiency of disclosure (with respect to original subject matter) cannot be made even if it relies on a prior art patent or printed publication — prior art patents/publications must be applied under an appropriate portion of 35 U.S.C. 102 and/or 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening patents or printed publications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections may be made in reexamination proceedings based on intervening patents or printed publications where the patent claims under reexamination are entitled only to the filing date of the patent and are not supported by an earlier foreign or United States patent application whose filing date is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervening patents/printed publications are available as prior art under precedent (e.g., In re Ruscetta, In re van Langenhoven). Examiner should determine entitlement to earlier filing dates (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 120 benefits) to assess whether intervening art is applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits/declarations to explain prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations or other written evidence which explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications in more detail may be considered in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304, any rejection must be based upon the prior art patents or printed publications as explained by the affidavits or declarations — the rejection cannot be based on the affidavits/declarations as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of admissions by the patent owner in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An admission per se may not be the basis for establishing a substantial new question of patentability at the order stage (consideration under 35 U.S.C. 303 is limited to patents and printed publications). However, an admission by the patent owner of record in the file or in a court record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication. After reexamination has been ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304, the examination on the merits is dictated by 35 U.S.C. 305 and admissions may be used to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim when applying prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 301(a)(2)/37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) permit submissions of patent owner statements filed in court or Office proceedings; if relied upon in a request, the requester must explain how the statement is used to determine claim meaning per 37 CFR 1.510(b)(2). Admissions in the record are to be considered in reexamination (may be used to interpret/modify prior art). Third parties may not submit patent owner admissions made outside the file or court record for order-stage consideration. Reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 may involve an admission by the patent owner without combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation rules and treatment in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: During reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 and under 35 U.S.C. 257, claims are given the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification (In re Yamamoto). Where there is related litigation and a federal court has made a judicial interpretation of a disputed claim term, the examiner should acknowledge the judicial interpretation and assess whether it is consistent with the broadest reasonable construction; if adopting a different construction the examiner should supply reasoning. For expired patents, claim construction pursuant to Phillips should be applied. The statutory presumption of validity (35 U.S.C. 282) has no application in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disclosure is amended, 35 U.S.C. 112 issues should be limited to amendatory matter; a limitation in an original patent claim that appears in a newly presented claim cannot be examined under 35 U.S.C. 112 unless the amendatory matter creates a new issue. Examiners should supply reasoning when differing from judicial constructions and may perform 35 U.S.C. 112 priority/written-description analyses where appropriate (see In re NTP).
